answer.evidence: Rows 0-14 are a wide corrugated tin roof plane with rust patches. It ends in a light front-edge line at row 15 (L=155 across columns), followed by dark eave shadow in rows 16-18 (L about 23-29). Below that, rows 19-46 form a south front face with a floor or sill strip at rows 43-46, and the silhouette narrows from 64 to 56 px under the overhanging roof. The roof is a sloped plane above an eave line and the front wall is 28 rows, so this is a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small tin shed with a corrugated roof, rust speckles, a hay bale and a door. Per-tile colour median is 16 against references at 18 and 11, and flat-fill coverage is 1%, so it is not flat by the numbers. Dark edge pixels are 16% neutral against 7-9% in the references. That is higher but still mostly tinted, so the outline reads as mixed. The 40 distinct colours are far below 185 and 66, which fits a small, simple object. The corrugated roof has vertical ribs with rust dots, giving about 4 steps against 5-6 on the reference tile roofs. The wall and interior areas are darker and simpler, with fewer highlight steps. The hay bale and door have little per-material shading. A careful artist would find it a bit thinner than the references, but it is not a sticker look and the texture is present.

styleAnswer.evidence: The shed is a small, simple building, but it matches the references on the measured facts. It has 16 distinct colours per 16x16 tile against 18 and 11 for the references, and 1% flat-fill coverage. Only 16% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean toward dark material tones (brown/rust beside the tin and wood) rather than a black sticker line. The corrugated roof has vertical ribs in several greys, with rust speckle for texture. The interior has hay bales shaded in several steps, and the diagonal-braced door and posts carry wood grain. Its 40 total colours are below the references' 66 and 185, but that fits a smaller object with a narrower palette. Roof and wall ramps reach about 4 steps against the references' 5-6, which is slightly shallow but acceptable. A careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, low tin shed: a corrugated grey roof with rust speckles, an open front showing hay bales and a tool, and a plank door on the right. The measured facts are close to the references. It has 16 colours per tile against 18 and 11, 1% flat-fill coverage, and only 16% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are mostly tinted, not a black sticker line. Its 40 distinct colours are well below the 185 and 66 of the references, and the picture agrees. The roof has about 4 grey steps with rust dots, which is fewer than the 6 steps of the tile roofs. The walls and interior are dark and fairly flat, with little grain, and the hay bales have only about 2-3 steps. The shed is small and simple, so the lower colour count is partly expected. Even so, it looks thinner and flatter than the references next to them, with less per-element shading, so I fail it when in doubt.
